title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.31851v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emotions are central drivers of human behavior, yet most behavioral models fail to capture their role in shaping perception, decision-making, and collective action. Application areas such as emergency response and public health are especially constrained by the lack of emotion-aware modeling. While large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into agent-based models (ABMs), little work has examined how to endow LLM agents with emotional reasoning or validated their ability to reproduce empirically observed emotional patterns. This study addresses this gap by introducing a hierarchical prompting framework that conditions LLM agents with demographic, psychological, and contextual cues to generate event-conditioned emotional responses to real-world events. We validate the resulting event-conditioned emotional responses against large-scale social media reaction data derived from the Social Science One Facebook URL Shares Dataset,

translated_title: 在合成社会模拟中利用大语言模型智能体建模事件条件化的情感表达响应
translated_abstract: 情感是人类行为的核心驱动力，然而大多数行为模型未能捕捉情感在塑造感知、决策和集体行动中的作用。应急响应和公共卫生等应用领域尤其受限于情感感知建模的缺失。尽管大语言模型（LLM）正日益被整合进基于智能体的模型（ABM）中，但很少有研究探讨如何赋予LLM智能体情感推理能力，或验证其再现实证观察到的情感模式的能力。本研究通过引入一个分层提示框架来填补这一空白，该框架利用人口统计、心理和情境线索对LLM智能体进行条件化，从而生成针对现实世界事件的事件条件化情感响应。我们使用源自Social Science One Facebook URL分享数据集的大规模社交媒体反应数据，对所生成的事件条件化情感响应进行了验证。
tldr: 本研究提出一个分层提示框架，通过人口统计、心理和情境线索赋予LLM智能体情感推理能力，使其生成事件条件化的情感响应，并利用大规模社交媒体数据验证了其再现真实情感模式的有效性。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a hierarchical prompting framework that endows LLM agents with emotional reasoning through demographic, psychological, and contextual cues to generate event-conditioned emotional responses, validated against large-scale social media reaction data.
